newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA probes SBC Warburg European share sale.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA probes SBC Warburg European share sale.

text.p: Investment bank SBC Warburg is being investigated by Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) over alleged mishandling of the sale of 300 million pounds of European shares for an investment trust, banking sources said on Wednesday.

The sources said the SFA investigation centred on the sharp fall of several European share prices in October after SBC Warburg carried out a series of share sales for Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust.
The sources said there had been an internal review at SBC Warburg and internal disciplinary action had been carried out. One executive recently left the company as a result.
The SFA was not immediately available for comment and SBC Warburg, a unit of the Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), would not comment on a report by the Financial Times about the probe.
The Financial Times said on Wednesday the share sale was believed to have resulted in a "multi-million pound" loss but banking sources said the figure was not that high.
The sources noted that SBC did not make a provision for the loss when it announced its 1996 earnings on Wednesday.
